packages.name: @tuix/process-manager
packages.summary: `@tuix/process-manager` starts, stops, and restarts child processes.
packages.purpose: Use this package to own process lifecycle in a Tuix app. The manager spawns work with Bun pipes or an interactive PTY. The production PTY path uses a `node-pty` backend. Set `pty: true` on a process config to open a TTY session.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when your app must run tools, servers, or shells. Use it when you need restart policy, logs, or metrics. Use it when a process needs a real terminal.
keyExports: createProcessManager — build and init a manager
ProcessManager / ProcessManagerLive — Effect service tag and layer

packages.name: @tuix/config
packages.summary: `@tuix/config` loads and stores app settings from many sources.
packages.purpose: Use this package to read config from files, environment, and defaults. It supports JSON, YAML, TOML, TypeScript, and env prefixes. You can validate values and watch files for change.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when an app needs hierarchical settings. Use it when you merge user, project, and env values. Use it when you need schema checks.
mainConcepts: Plugin commands for get and set
keyExports: loadConfig — load standard user and project config
config — simple, standard, cli, env, and file helpers
ConfigPlugin — JSX plugin with get, set, list, import, export

example.code:
import { createConfig, loadConfig } from '@tuix/config'

const cfg = await createConfig()
  .name('myapp')
  .defaults({ logger: { level: 'info' } })
  .withUserConfig()
  .withProjectConfig()
  .envPrefix('MYAPP_')
  .build()

const level = cfg.get<string>('logger.level')

packages.name: @tuix/testing
packages.summary: `@tuix/testing` provides harnesses, snapshots, and e2e PTY tests.
packages.purpose: Use this package to test Tuix components and CLI sessions. `createTestHarness` runs MVU components with mock services. The e2e harness spawns a real process with `node-pty` for keys and text waits.
packages.whenToUse: Use it for unit tests of views and updates. Use it for snapshot and performance checks. Use it for full terminal e2e flows.
keyExports: createTestHarness — MVU component harness with mock services
testComponent — run init, update, and view tests
createTestHarness (e2e) — PTY session for CLI e2e
runTest — run an Effect test against a PTY session
expectMatchSnapshot — compare view output to a snapshot

packages.name: @tuix/bin
packages.summary: `@tuix/bin` is the `tuix` CLI entry for version, help, and dashboard.
packages.purpose: Use this package as the official command line app. It shows a welcome screen by default. Commands cover version info, interactive help, and a live system dashboard.
packages.whenToUse: Use it to run the shipped Tuix CLI. Use it as a sample of app commands and plugins. Use it when you need a ready demo surface.
keyExports: VersionCommand — show version and system info

packages.name: @tuix/logger
packages.summary: `@tuix/logger` writes structured logs to console, file, stream, or HTTP.
packages.purpose: Use this package for levels, formatters, and transports. It provides pretty, JSON, compact, and CLI formats. Presets cover development, production, CLI, and remote sinks.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when the app must log with levels and context. Use it when you need file or remote output. Use it when you need a live log view.

example.code:
import { createConsoleLogger } from '@tuix/logger'
import { Effect } from 'effect'

const log = createConsoleLogger('info', { showEmoji: true })
await Effect.runPromise(log.info('server ready', { port: 3000 }))

packages.name: @tuix/coordination
packages.summary: `@tuix/coordination` runs workflows, event choreography, and recovery.
packages.purpose: Use this package to coordinate multi-module work. The orchestrator runs centralized workflows. The choreographer links events without tight coupling. Stream tools and recovery helpers keep flows stable.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when modules must share long event flows. Use it when you need retries and recovery. Use it when stream load needs control.

packages.name: @tuix/debug
packages.summary: `@tuix/debug` provides a debug TUI for scopes, events, state, and performance.
packages.purpose: Use this package to inspect runtime behavior in the terminal. It stores debug events and exposes tabs for scopes, events, state, and performance. MVU hooks wire the store into the loop.
packages.whenToUse: Use it while you build or fix a Tuix app. Use it when you need event and state inspection. Use it when render cost must be visible.
keyExports: MVU integration exports — wire debug into the loop

example.code:
import { createDebugLogger } from '@tuix/debug'

const dbg = createDebugLogger('my-module', { color: '36' })
dbg.info('update started')
dbg.error('update failed', { code: 500 })

packages.name: @tuix/docs
packages.summary: `@tuix/docs` extracts command docs and shows an interactive help explorer.
packages.purpose: Use this package to read docs from JSX commands and plugins. Generators write Markdown or plain help text. `HelpExplorer` lets users browse commands with the keyboard.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when your CLI needs in-app help. Use it when you want docs from the same command tree. Use it when you export Markdown for a site.
keyExports: extractAppDoc — build app docs from JSX
generateAppMarkdown — write Markdown for an app
generateCommandHelp — plain text help for a command

packages.name: @tuix/telemetry
packages.summary: `@tuix/telemetry` collects opt-in events, errors, and performance metrics.
packages.purpose: Use this package only when the user opts in. Collectors capture events, errors, and performance data. Transports send batches to HTTP or write them to files.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when product metrics must stay opt-in. Use it when you need error or timing reports. Use it when you ship to HTTP or local files.

packages.name: @tuix/update
packages.summary: `@tuix/update` checks package versions and can show an update banner.
packages.purpose: Use this package to compare the current version to a remote source. Checkers support npm, GitHub releases, and custom URLs. The plugin can auto-check and render a banner.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when a CLI should notify users of new versions. Use it when you publish on npm or GitHub. Use it when you need a custom check endpoint.

packages.name: @tuix/app-presets
packages.summary: `@tuix/app-presets` supplies module factory presets for runtime bootstrap.
packages.purpose: Use this package to inject higher-layer modules without wrong dependency edges. Factories cover config, logger, process manager, and coordination. The standard preset returns a safe default set.
packages.whenToUse: Use it when you call runtime bootstrap with extra modules. Use it when you want config and logger by default. Use it when you opt into process manager or coordination.
mainConcepts: Config, logger, process manager, coordination factories
keyExports: StandardPresetOptions — toggle flags for the standard set
